svg.aria-label: Diagram setting the default AWS Lambda compute type against Lambda Managed Instances. On the default compute type, one execution environment runs one invocation at a time, scaling happens on demand as invocations arrive so cold starts occur, billing is per gigabyte-second of execution duration, and the timeout is fifteen minutes on every invocation path. On Managed Instances, one execution environment handles several invocations simultaneously, scaling is asynchronous based on CPU utilisation so cold starts are eliminated but traffic that more than doubles within five minutes may be throttled, billing is standard EC2 instance pricing plus a fifteen percent management fee plus twenty cents per million requests with no separate duration charge, and the timeout is ninety minutes for asynchronous and event source mapping invocations while synchronous invocations remain at fifteen. A band across the bottom records that the capacity provider is the security boundary so all functions assigned to one must be mutually trusted, gated by the lambda PassCapacityProvider permission.
svg.title: The Lambda timeout moved because the billing unit did
svg.text: Duration stopped being the meter, so a long invocation stopped being priced like one
Two compute types, and the ninety minutes belongs to only one of them — on only one invocation path.
Needs thread safety and context isolation.
No cold starts. Doubling in 5 min may throttle.
No separate duration charge. Idle still bills.
Timeout: 90 minutes — async and ESM only
Synchronous invocations keep the 15-minute maximum, on both compute types
Which is coherent: the modes that got the increase are the ones with a queue in front and a retry story behind, where nobody is holding a connection open.
And a boundary that did not exist before
A capacity provider is the security boundary: all functions assigned to the same one must be mutually trusted, gated by lambda:PassCapacityProvider.
